processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Ingots with nominal composition Fe-35Mn-15Al-5Cu (at.%) produced by melting high-purity (>99.9 %) raw materials in a vacuum induction furnace under argon.
Homogenized ingots hot-rolled into plates with a thickness of 4 mm.
Plates cut into 10 × 5 × 2 mm³ samples by electrical discharge machining for Vickers hardness measurements and microstructure characterizations.
Solution-treated at 1100 °C for 10 min under argon, followed by oil quenching (parent process of the aging treatment).
Defining aging treatment of this sample: 15Al alloy aged at 650 °C for 10 h, followed by water quenching.

structures.overall_structure: For the 15Al alloy aged at 650 °C the α (BCC) matrix had almost completely transformed into β-Mn (the transformation being complete within ~1 h at 600 °C and above), with abundant fine BCC and FCC precipitates distributed within the β-Mn; untransformed α regions were no longer observed at 650 °C.

phases_present.morphology: matrix formed by the α → β-Mn transformation
fine particles distributed at the interfaces between β-Mn
fine particles within β-Mn / at β-Mn interfaces

precipitates.distribution: at the interfaces between β-Mn / within β-Mn

interfaces.phase_evolution: α → α + FCC Cu-rich phase → α-Mn + β-Mn + BCC phase → β-Mn + BCC phase + FCC Cu-rich phase
interfaces.interface_notes: During growth, β-Mn (an Mn-rich phase) expels Fe, Al and Cu to the surroundings; the expelled Al enriches BCC-stabilizing element around the interfaces forming the new BCC phase, while limited Cu solubility leads to the FCC Cu-rich phase. The content of FCC Cu-rich phase between β-Mn interfaces decreased gradually with increasing Al content.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Vickers microhardness measured on an HVS-1000 digital microhardness tester with a load of 9.8 N for 15 s; each sample tested 5 times and averaged.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: load of 9.8 N for 15 s; each sample tested 5 times and hardness reported as the average of 5 measurements; electrolytically polished samples (10 % perchloric acid + 90 % ethanol)
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure Vickers hardness of the 15Al alloy after aging treatments
characterization_methods.key_findings: 15Al alloy aged at 650 °C for 10 h has a Vickers hardness of 842.3 ± 3.7 HV

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: ZEISS Sigma 300 SEM operated at 5 kV
characterization_methods.purpose: Identify the precipitation of secondary phases (α-Mn and β-Mn) and new precipitates in aged samples
characterization_methods.key_findings: For the 15Al alloy, when aged at 600 °C and above the α matrix had almost completely transformed into β-Mn within just 1 h and abundant fine precipitates (BCC and FCC) were observed within the β-Mn; the rate of β-Mn precipitation and growth was accelerated with increasing aging temperature

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: GeminiSEM 300 SEM; scanning step size 1.5 μm for low magnification and 0.05 μm for high magnification
characterization_methods.purpose: Clarify the microstructural origin of the rapid aging hardening behaviour (phase identification)
characterization_methods.key_findings: For the 15Al alloy, following aging at 650 °C the untransformed α regions were no longer observed and a new FCC phase was distributed in β-Mn; at 550 °C/6 h a new fine BCC phase was present within β-Mn — demonstrating the α→β-Mn transformation plus late BCC and FCC precipitation

unmapped_findings: Chemical composition of the 15Al (Fe-35Mn-15Al-5Cu) alloy measured by EDS (at.%, Table 1): Fe 44.6, Mn 35.2, Al 15.0, Cu 5.2 (equivalently Fe-35.2Mn-15.0Al-5.2Cu).

For the 15Al alloy, the solution-treated (1100 °C/10 min, oil quenched) Vickers hardness baseline was 253.4 ± 2.1 HV (Table 2), the lowest hardness of the ultrawide 253.4–965.6 HV window achieved across the alloy series.
For the 15Al alloy, hardness after aging at 625 °C and 650 °C stabilized between 800 HV and 900 HV with prolonged aging time (this regime contains the 650 °C/10 h condition of 842.3 ± 3.7 HV).

The peak hardness of the 15Al alloy was 965.6 ± 7.6 HV (600 °C/6 h), a condition distinct from this 650 °C/10 h sample; that peak hardness combined with the 6.85 g/cm³ density gives the Fe-35.2Mn-15Al-5.2Cu alloy an ultra-high specific hardness of 141 HV·cm³/g (reported as > 140 HV·cm³/g).

Fracture toughness K_IC of 8.6 MPa·m^1/2 (with an average indentation crack length of 18 μm) was reported for the 15Al alloy at its peak hardness of 965.6 HV (600 °C/6 h), not for the 650 °C/10 h condition.

The intrinsic β-Mn nanoindentation hardness of the hardest 15Al sample (600 °C/6 h) was 12.1 ± 0.3 GPa, and its SEM-EDS β-Mn composition was Mn 36.8 at.%, Al 14.3 at.%, Cu 2.8 at.% — values belonging to the peak-hardness condition, not this 650 °C/10 h sample.
